{{Short description|Unsolved problem in number theory}}
{{unsolved|mathematics|Must the [[Galois cohomology]] set of a [[simply connected space|simply connected]], [[semisimple algebraic group]] over a [[perfect field]] of [[cohomological dimension]] at most 2 always equal zero?}}

In [[mathematics]], specifically [[number theory]], '''Serre's conjecture II''' is the statement that if ''G'' is a [[simply connected space|simply connected]], [[semisimple algebraic group]] over a [[perfect field]] ''F'' of [[cohomological dimension]] at most 2, then the [[Galois cohomology]] set ''H''<sup>1</sup>(''F'',&nbsp;''G'') is zero.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Serre|first=Jean-Pierre|title=Cohomologie galoisienne des groupes algébriques linéaires|year=1962|pages=53–68|journal=Colloque sur la théorie des groupes algébriques, Bruxelles|oclc=1708914|trans-title=Galois cohomology of linear algebraic groups}}</ref><ref name="CG">{{cite book |last=Serre |first=Jean-Pierre |title=Cohomologie galoisienne |publisher=Springer Berlin, Heidelberg |year=1994 |orig-year=1964 |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |volume=5 |edition=5th |isbn=978-3-540-58002-7|doi=10.1007/BFb0108758}}</ref> It was proposed by [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] in 1962, as an higher-dimension equivalent of his conjecture I (which was later proven).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Izquierdo |first1=Diego |last2=Lucchini Arteche |first2=Giancarlo |date=2025-11-01 |title=Transfer principles for Galois cohomology and Serre's conjecture II |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000187082500430X |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=480 |article-number=110532 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2025.110532 |issn=0001-8708|arxiv=2308.00903}}</ref> 

A converse of the conjecture holds: if the field ''F'' is perfect and if the cohomology set ''H''<sup>1</sup>(''F'',&nbsp;''G'') is zero for every semisimple, simply connected algebraic group ''G,'' then the ''p''-cohomological dimension of ''F'' is at most 2 for every [[Prime number|prime]] ''p''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Serre |first=Jean-Pierre |date=1995 |title=Cohomologie galoisienne : progrès et problèmes |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/?id=SB_1993-1994__36__229_0 |journal=Astérisque |volume=227 |pages=229–247 |mr=1321649 |zbl=0837.12003}}</ref> The conjecture has been proven for all groups over all perfect fields; however, it remains open for [[Anisotropy|anisotropic]] [[E6 (mathematics)|E6]], [[E7 (mathematics)|E7]] and [[E8 (mathematics)|E8]] groups and [[Triality|trialitarian]] [[Klein four-group|D4]] group over imperfect fields.

==Known cases==

The conjecture holds in the case where ''F'' is a [[local field]] (such as [[p-adic number|p-adic field]]), a [[global field]] with no real [[Embedding|embeddings]] (such as '''Q'''({{radic|−1}})) or a [[totally imaginary number field]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kneser |first=Martin |date=1965-02-01 |title=Galois-Kohomologie halbeinfacher algebraischer Gruppen überp-adischen Körpern. I |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01112691 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |language=de |volume=88 |issue=1 |pages=40–47 |doi=10.1007/BF01112691 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kneser |first=Martin |date=1965-06-01 |title=Galois-Kohomologie halbeinfacher algebraischer Gruppen über p-adischen Körpern. II |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02116869 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |language=de |volume=89 |issue=3 |pages=250–272 |doi=10.1007/BF02116869 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This is a special case of the [[Martin Kneser|Kneser]]–[[Günter Harder|Harder]]–Chernousov [[Hasse principle]] for [[Algebraic group|algebraic groups]] over global fields. (Note that such fields do indeed have cohomological dimension at most&nbsp;2.<ref name="CG" />) 
The conjecture holds when ''F'' is [[Finitely generated group|finitely generated]] over [[Complex number|complex numbers]] and has [[transcendence degree]] at most&nbsp;2. The conjecture also holds for l-special fields, [[Complete valued field|complete valued fields]] and [[Function field of an algebraic variety|function fields]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=de Jong|first1=A. J.|last2=He|first2=Xuhua|last3=Starr|first3=Jason Michael|eprint=0809.5224|title=Families of rationally simply connected varieties over surfaces and torsors for semisimple groups|year=2008|class=math.AG}}</ref>

The conjecture is known to hold for certain groups&nbsp;''G''. For [[Special linear group|special linear groups]], it is a consequence of the [[Merkurjev–Suslin theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Merkurjev|first1=A. S.|author-link=Alexander Merkurjev|last2=Suslin|first2=A. A.|author2-link=Andrei Suslin|title=K-cohomology of Severi-Brauer varieties and the norm-residue homomorphism|journal=Math. USSR Izvestiya|volume=21|year=1983|issue=2|pages=307–340|doi=10.1070/im1983v021n02abeh001793|bibcode=1983IzMat..21..307M}}</ref> Building on this result, the conjecture holds if ''G'' is a [[classical group]] (type [[A-group|A]], B, [[C-group|C]] or D with no [[triality]]); or a group of type [[F4 (mathematics)|F4]] and [[G2 (mathematics)|G2]] on a [[perfect field]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bayer-Fluckiger|first1=Eva|last2=Parimala|first2=Raman|title=Galois cohomology of the classical groups over fields of cohomological dimension&nbsp;≤&nbsp;2|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|year=1995|volume=122|issue=1 |pages=195–229 | doi = 10.1007/BF01231443 |bibcode=1995InMat.122..195B|s2cid=124673233|url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/214646 |author-link=Eva Bayer-Fluckiger|author-link2=Raman Parimala}}</ref> The conjecture also holds for classical groups over imperfect fields.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berhuy |first=Grégory |last2=Frings |first2=Christoph |last3=Tignol |first3=Jean-Pierre |author-link3=Jean-Pierre Tignol |date=2007-11-01 |title=Galois cohomology of the classical groups over imperfect fields |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002240490700028X |journal=Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra |volume=211 |issue=2 |pages=307–341 |doi=10.1016/j.jpaa.2007.01.001 |doi-access=free|s2cid=122036284|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Over perfect fields, the conjecture also holds if ''G'' is an [[Isotropy|isotropic]] or [[Quasi-split group|quasi-split]] [[exceptional Lie group|exceptional group]] (except for [[E8 (mathematics)|E8]]);<ref>{{cite journal|last=Gille|first=Philippe|title=Cohomologie galoisienne des groupes quasi-déployés sur des corps de dimension cohomologique&nbsp;≤&nbsp;2|journal=Compositio Mathematica|year=2001|volume=125|issue=3|pages=283–325|doi=10.1023/A:1002473132282|s2cid=124765999|doi-access=free|language=fr|trans-title=Galois cohomology of quasi-split groups over fields of cohomological dimension ≤ 2}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Gille|first=Philippe|title=Groupes algébriques semi-simples en dimension cohomologique ≤2|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|year=2019|volume=2238|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-17272-5|isbn=978-3-030-17271-8 }}</ref> or a [[pseudo-reductive group]].<ref>{{Citation |last=Nguyen |first=Mac Nam Trung |title=Serre conjecture II for pseudo-reductive groups |date=2026-03-09 |url=http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08061 |access-date=2026-08-18 |publisher=arXiv |doi=10.48550/arXiv.2603.08061 |s2cid=286377008|arxiv=2603.08061|doi-access=free}}</ref>
